meaning: True iff the referenced group is filled. For a repeatable group this means the repeat row EXISTS — an empty, freshly created row counts as filled.

an enclosing GroupFilled(Group) counts as referencing the rule's error field (no MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED)

meaning: Maps an enumeration field's value to its value in the named category: [Field -> Category]. The model pairs category values positionally with the enum values; comparisons run against the category's (distinct) value domain.
constraints: the left operand must be an enumeration field (MVK_NO_ENUMERATION otherwise)
the category must be declared on that field's enumeration (MVK_CATEGORY_UNKOWN — kernel's spelling)
gotchas: compare against CATEGORY values, not the enum's own values — '[Priority -> SpeedClass] == "EXPRESS"' is rejected because EXPRESS is an enum value, not a SpeedClass value
the arrow is the same symbol in every condition language

validExample.note: fires when the priority's speed class is FAST

invalidExample.fix: EXPRESS is an enum value; compare to a SpeedClass category value (NORMAL/FAST)

meaning: The boolean/confirm constant 'true'. Booleans compare to True/False; confirm fields compare ONLY to True (== / !=).
constraints: usable in equality comparisons against boolean fields (== / !=) and confirm fields (== / != True only)
gotchas: an UNSET boolean makes the comparison not-evaluated (neither true nor false) — guard with FieldFilled when that matters
an unset confirm counts as not confirmed, so [Confirm] != True is the idiom for 'not confirmed'

validExample.note: fires when the boolean is set and true

invalidExample.fix: a boolean compares only to True/False or another boolean field, never to a string

meaning: The boolean constant 'false'. Legal against boolean fields only — a confirm field never compares to False.
constraints: usable in equality comparisons against boolean fields only
gotchas: confirm fields compare only to True — [Confirm] == False is rejected; use [Confirm] != True for 'not confirmed'

validExample.note: fires when the boolean is set and false

invalidExample.fix: a confirm compares only to True (or another confirm field) — use [TermsConfirmed] != True

meaning: The character length of a string field's value.
constraints: the operand must be a string field
gotchas: applying Length to a non-string field is a type error

validExample.note: fires when CustomerName is longer than 10 characters

invalidExample.fix: Length needs a string field, not a number

meaning: True iff the string field's whole value matches the regular expression (anchored).
constraints: the left side must be a bare string field value — no expressions, no constants, no enums
the right side must be a string constant holding a valid regex
only the regex subset portable across the kernel's target languages is accepted (e.g. lookbehind is rejected although Java-valid)
gotchas: the match is anchored over the WHOLE value — '@' does not find an @ somewhere, use '.*@.*'
in DSL string literals a backslash is a plain character and an embedded quote is doubled (""), so regex character classes like \d are written as-is
a backtracking-prone pattern such as (a+)+ is a performance/security risk (KERNEL-SEMANTICS §7)

validExample.note: fires when ProductCode has the legacy XX-9999 format

invalidExample.fix: pattern comparison works on string fields only

meaning: True iff the string field's whole value does NOT match the regular expression (anchored).
constraints: the left side must be a bare string field value — no expressions, no constants, no enums
the right side must be a string constant holding a valid regex
only the regex subset portable across the kernel's target languages is accepted
gotchas: an empty field is not evaluated — guard with FieldFilled when the rule should fire only on present-but-malformed values

validExample.note: fires when a present postal code is not exactly five digits

invalidExample.fix: the right side must be a valid (portable-subset) regular expression
